# Kodeverse: what a ten-dollar coding plan gets you OpenCode Go and Command Code GOAT compared model by model. Both cost ten dollars a month. Every figure is read from the vendor pages and stamped with the date it was read. The page is a static Astro build. The [method](#how-the-numbers-are-read), the [findings](#the-short-answer) and the engineering notes are below. To run it: `bun run build` then `bun run serve`, and open http://127.0.0.1:8787. ## The question Same price. Do the two plans give the same usable allowance, and if not, which one gives more on the models I actually use? ## The short answer - They differ. Across the 26 models both plans publish an allowance for, Command Code GOAT leads on 14 models, OpenCode Go leads on 9, and 3 are level. - The plans cap differently. OpenCode Go derives each window from the model's own monthly limit: 20% for five hours, 50% for a week. Command Code GOAT states flat caps: $14 for five hours and $35 for a week, on every model. - Token prices barely differ. Where they do, the comparison shows both rates per model, so the rest of the comparison is allowance alone. - The best case is the same on both plans: $80 of monthly credit on one model. The five-hour cap is the number a user actually meets, and that is where the plans part company. - The widest single gap is $40 of monthly credit, on MiMo-V2.6-Flash and on the Muse Spark contributor models. Figures as read on the date stamped in the footer of the page. The vendors move their pages without notice, so treat the plan pages as the contract and this document as a dated reading of them. ## How the numbers are read 1. Both vendor pages are read directly. OpenCode answers markdown when asked, which is the smaller and easier parse. Command Code publishes HTML tables. 2. Each catalogue is parsed into one row per model: four token rates, a monthly credit, the vendor's own request estimates per window, and any promotion printed beside the rate. 3. The two catalogues are merged on a normalised model key. The key strips the vendor's own formatting, so "Tencent Hy4 Preview" and "Hy4 preview" are one model. The cheapest tier listed for a key wins, so off-peak and smaller context variants do not double-count. 4. Caps are applied per plan, read from the plan's own rule. A flat cap is the smaller of the allowance and the cap. A derived cap is the model limit times the share. An unlimited allowance keeps unlimited caps. 5. A model is comparable only when both plans publish the figure on screen. A model one plan merely carries has nothing to compare, so it stays out of the table instead of arriving as a row of dashes. 26 of the 64 catalogued models are comparable. ## The pipeline ```mermaid flowchart LR OC["opencode.ai Go page
(markdown)"] --> PARSE["parsers.ts
one row per model"] CC["commandcode.ai GOAT page
(html)"] --> PARSE PARSE --> MERGE["merge.ts
keys normalised, caps applied"] MERGE --> JSON[("src/data/plans.json
the baked figures")] JSON --> BUILD["astro build"] BUILD --> PAGE["dist/index.html
head, JSON-LD, sitemap"] PAGE --> READER["Reader"] READER -->|"Refresh, one click"| ROUTE{"read route"} ROUTE -->|"same-origin when served"| PROXY["/api/raw
loopback allow list"] ROUTE -->|"any other origin"| RELAY["reader service
plus a second relay"] PROXY --> PARSE RELAY --> PARSE READER -->|"one snapshot per day"| LOG[("localStorage
30-day changelog")] GATE["bun scripts/verify.ts
fixtures, merge, caps, relay shape"] --> PARSE SMOKE["bun scripts/browser-smoke.mjs
real browser, live refresh"] --> PAGE UNIT["bun run test
62 unit tests over the rules"] --> RULES["compare, parsers,
merge, changelog, format"] ``` ## Why a static page and a refresh button - Nothing to read needs a server. The page is a static build with the figures baked in at build time. - Refresh is one click, and the read does not depend on any one server. When the page is served by `bun run serve`, the read goes to a same-origin route that is loopback-only and fixed to an allow list, so no third party is in the loop. From any other origin the read falls back to public readers: Command Code is read directly because it sends `Access-Control-Allow-Origin`, and opencode.ai, which sends none, is read through a reader service that echoes the origin back. - A refresh fails closed. A reply that comes back missing a plan, missing most of the catalogue, or with too few comparable models is refused, and the figures on screen stay the ones the last build read. - Every refresh is audit-logged. The page keeps one snapshot per day for thirty days in the browser and diffs the live figures against the most recent day. The log is a dialog behind a nav icon, not a section: a reader opens it when they wonder what moved, and it never takes a place in the page's argument. ## Page metadata and SEO The head is built once in `src/layouts/main.astro`, from one identity block, so the tags, the JSON-LD and the sitemap cannot disagree. - Title, description, keywords, authors, creator and publisher. - `metadataBase` and a canonical url, with `hreflang` alternates for the default and English locales. - Open Graph complete: type, site name, locale, title, description, url, and a image with type, width, height and alt text. Twitter uses the same card. - Icons: `brand.webp` as the favicon and the apple touch icon, plus a web manifest. - Robots: indexable, followed, full-size image previews, in the head and in `robots.txt`. - schema.org structured data as JSON-LD: Organization, WebSite, WebPage and a Dataset whose `dateModified` is the same read stamp the footer shows. - `sitemap.xml` with a `lastmod` from that stamp. Absolute urls come from one environment variable. Set it before building: ``` SITE_URL=https://your-domain bun run build ``` Without it the build still succeeds, and the head omits only the absolute urls. Cabinet Grotesk is self-hosted in `public/fonts`, so no font is fetched from a third party at read time. ## How correctness is checked Three layers, from the cheapest to the closest to the reader. - `bun run test` is the unit gate. 62 tests over the pure library: the comparison rules (who leads, by how much, what a tie is, which models are comparable), the cell readers and both vendor parsers, the merge and its cap rules, the refresh guard, the changelog diff and history window, and the display formatting. Every expected value is a literal. - `bun run verify` is the data gate. It checks the baked data, both parsers against the saved vendor fixtures, the merge and its cap rules, the changelog diff, and the shape of the relay. A truncated read must still parse whole. - `bun run smoke` drives the built page in a real browser against the local server. It exercises the filter, both comparison dimensions, paging, the theme, and a live refresh, and it fails on any uncaught page error. - Numbers are never invented. Every figure on the page comes from the vendor pages, and the read date sits in the footer. ## Layout ``` src/ data/plans.json the baked figures: scripts/update.ts writes, the page reads lib/ parsers, merge, comparison rules, changelog, refresh, format components/compare/ one file per section, plus the shared bits and view state components/ui/ shadcn components pages/index.astro the page pages/robots.txt.ts and sitemap.xml.ts, built from the same read stamp layouts/main.astro the shell: head, mark sprite, theme bootstrap, toaster scripts/ update.ts fetch both vendor docs, parse, write src/data/plans.json serve.mjs serve dist/ and the read proxy at http://127.0.0.1:8787 verify.ts the gate: data, parsers, merge, changelog, serve contract browser-smoke.mjs drive the built page in a real browser vendor/ the two vendor pages, kept as fixtures for verify.ts ``` ## Commands ``` bun install bun run update # re-read both vendors, rewrite src/data/plans.json bun run build # static build to dist/ bun run serve # http://127.0.0.1:8787 with the read proxy bun run dev # astro dev bun run lint # oxlint bun run fmt # oxfmt bun run check # lint + fmt:check bun run typecheck # astro check bun run test # vitest, the unit gate bun run verify # the gate (needs a build in dist/) bun run smoke # browser smoke against a running serve.mjs ``` ## Known limits - Request estimates are each vendor's own. The vendors assume different tokens per request, so a request column is read on its own and never summed across plans as if the units matched. - A refresh reads the pages the allow list names. A vendor that moves a plan to a new url stops being read until the list is updated. - The figures are as current as the last read. The footer states that date and warns once the reading is more than six hours old. - No translated variant exists, so the only `hreflang` alternates are the default and English.

# Go OpenCode Go gives you reliable access to popular open coding models, with two monthly plans: | Plan | Price | Included usage | | ----------- | ------------- | ------------------------------------------- | | **Go** | **$10/month** | Lower-cost access to the models below | | **Go Plus** | **$40/month** | Higher usage limits across the models below | Go works like any other provider in OpenCode. You subscribe to OpenCode Go and get your API key. It's **completely optional** and you don't need it to use OpenCode. The service is designed primarily for international users and provides stable global access. ## How it works 1. Sign in to the [OpenCode Console](https://opencode.ai/console), subscribe to Go or Go Plus, add your billing details, and copy your API key. 2. Run `/connect` in the TUI, select **OpenCode Go**, and paste your API key. ```text /connect ``` 3. Run `/models` to select a model available through Go. ```text /models ``` Go and Go Plus are for workspaces with a single member, such as the **Personal** workspace created when you sign up. A workspace with a Go subscription cannot invite members. The current list of models includes: - **Grok 4.7** - **GLM-5.3-Flash** - **GLM-5.3** - **GLM-5.2** - **GPT 6 Luna** - **GPT 5.6 Luna** - **Claude Haiku 5.5** - **Gemini 4 Argon Contributor** - **Kimi K3.1 Pro** - **Kimi K3** - **Kimi K2.7 Code** - **LongCat-2.0** - **LongCat 2.5 Preview Free** (limited time) - **Step 5 Preview** - **Beam Free** (limited time, limited regions) - **MiMo-V2.6-Flash** - **MiMo-V2.6-Pro** - **MiMo-V2.5** - **MiMo-V2.5-Pro** - **MiniMax M3.1 Flash** - **MiniMax M3** - **Muse Spark 1.3 Contributor** ([limited regions](https://ai.developer.meta.com/legal/geographic-use-policy)) - **Muse Spark 1.2 Contributor** ([limited regions](https://ai.developer.meta.com/legal/geographic-use-policy)) - **Qwen3.8 Max** - **Qwen3.8 Flash** - **Qwen3.7 Plus** - **DeepSeek V4.1 Flash** - **DeepSeek V4 Pro** - **Hy4 preview** - **Hy3** The list of models may change as we test and add new ones. ### Enable restricted models Workspace privacy settings apply to Go. By default, paid endpoints that train on request data are blocked, and allowed regions are **Europe & United States**. Workspaces without saved privacy settings also allow **Global** for requests from China. In **Settings › Privacy**, an owner or admin can enable: - **DeepSeek V4.1 Flash and V4 Pro:** select **Global** under **Regions**. - **Gemini 4 Argon Contributor, Muse Spark 1.3 Contributor, and Muse Spark 1.2 Contributor:** turn on **Allow paid endpoints that train on request data**. See [Privacy](#privacy) for each model's training and retention terms. ## Where can I use it? OpenCode Go is designed for [OpenCode](https://opencode.ai) and other coding agents that produce similar types of requests. Traffic is monitored for abuse that degrades the experience for other users. Your client should: 1. Send typical coding agent traffic 2. Identify itself with its own user agent, such as `my-coding-agent/1.0`, rather than a generic SDK or HTTP-library name. 3. Send a stable session ID in `x-opencode-session` for each conversation so we can optimize routing and prompt caching. See [Harnesses](/console/harnesses) to set up Go in Claude Code, Codex, Hermes, Pi, and Raycast. ### Validated clients Besides OpenCode, the following clients have been validated to work properly with OpenCode Go, although we do not guarantee that they will continue to work in the future. | Client | Session support | | ----------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | **Hermes** | Update to **v0.21.6 or later**, which sends the header on main and auxiliary OpenCode requests ([PR #101864](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/101864)). | | **Claude Code** | Go recognizes its native session header. No custom-header wrapper is needed. | | **Codex** | Go recognizes its native session header. Some versions and proxy setups still omit it; preserve the session header when forwarding requests. | | **ZCode** | Go recognizes its native session header. Our [request for `x-opencode-session`](https://github.com/zai-org/feedback/issues/492) remains open, but it is no longer necessary to send that specific header. | | **Pi** | Current builds send session information for OpenCode. Update older installations. | | **jcode** | Update to **v0.81.6 or later**, which includes the [session-header fix](https://github.com/1jehuang/jcode/issues/1167). | | **Kilo Code CLI** | Builds containing [PR #13752](https://github.com/Kilo-Org/kilocode/pull/13752) restore OpenCode session headers. This fix covers the CLI, not the VS Code extension. See [issue #13723](https://github.com/Kilo-Org/kilocode/issues/13723). | ### Known problematic clients These clients have missing or incomplete session support in the versions we investigated. The linked reports track fixes and workarounds. | Client | Status and tracking | | ----------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | | **DeepSeek Harness** | Session information arrives on some model paths, but is missing on others. We recognize its native header; the remaining work is to send it across all adapters. [Discussion #5495](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/discussions/5495). | | **GitHub Copilot Chat** | Automatic session-header support is requested in [VS Code issue #334186](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/334186). | | **Kimi Code** | The session-header request in [issue #3506](https://github.com/MoonshotAI/kimi-code/issues/3506) was closed as not planned. | | **MiMo Code** | [Issue #2317](https://github.com/XiaomiMiMo/MiMo-Code/issues/2317) is closed, and [PR #2327](https://github.com/XiaomiMiMo/MiMo-Code/pull/2327) was closed without merging. | ## Usage limits Usage limits are defined as monthly dollar amounts. The table below shows the monthly limit for each plan and the token costs for each model. Token pricing is the same for Go and Go Plus. Each model has the following usage limits: 5-hour — 20% of the monthly limit; weekly — 50%; and monthly — 100%. The current agreement is valid through October 31, 2026. ## Background Open models have gotten really good. They now reach performance close to proprietary models for coding tasks. Because many providers can serve them competitively, they are usually far cheaper. However, getting reliable, low latency access to them can be difficult. Providers vary in quality and availability. We tested a select group of models and providers that work well with OpenCode. To fix this, we did a couple of things: 1. We tested a select group of open models and talked to their teams about how to best run them. 2. We worked with a few providers to make sure these were being served correctly. 3. We benchmarked the combination of the model/provider and came up with a list that we feel good recommending. Both Go and Go Plus provide access to these models; choose the plan that fits how much you use them. ## Goals We created OpenCode Go to: 1. Make AI coding **accessible** to more people with a low cost subscription. 2. Provide **reliable** access to the best open coding models. 3. Curate models that are **tested and benchmarked** for coding agent use. 4. Have **no lock-in** by allowing you to use any other provider with OpenCode as well.
